title: No 'Explain fit' reasoning affordance on the job→candidates shortlist surface
expected: Journey DoD: each shortlisted candidate carries reasoning (verdict + strengths + gaps + interview probes) on the ranked list Petra hands a manager.
got: RecruiterCandidates rows show score/confidence/skills/KO only. /api/match/reasoning is invoked from exactly two places app-wide: the Match tab card (candidate→jobs, the inverse direction — per candidate she must re-run Match and re-find the role in their list) and the Matrix cell popover (Insights group, outside Petra's and Jana's surface bindings; reachable via Pipeline's 'Rank candidates' deep-link).
scope_note: Co-signed by jana-sourcer ('a reason I'd repeat to a hiring manager') and katerina-ta-analytics. Backend is ready: runReasoning already accepts profileId|analysisSlug + jobId (app/_lib/reasoning-run.ts:32-48), so the shortlist card could call it directly.
suggested_acceptance: On the job's candidates list, each eligible row exposes an 'Explain fit' action that returns the cached/LLM verdict for (this candidate, this job) without leaving the modal.
l2_priority: Time a recruiter assembling top-5 WITH reasoning via the Match-tab detour; confirm no hidden path exists in the modal.

title: Legacy-analysis candidates scored under archetype 'bau' on the job-side shortlist but fail-closed 'unknown' on the Match/reasoning path
expected: The same candidate resolves to the same archetype (and thus the same KO gates and fairness shield) on every surface.
got: candidate-pool.ts poolEntryFromAnalysis hardcodes archetype:'bau' for an analysis without a v2 profile, applying the seniority KO floor and stripping the early-career fairness shield — the exact hazard match-candidate.ts documents and avoids with its 'unknown' sentinel (no seniority auto-KO, neutral weights). A student/switcher can be KO'd on the Jobs shortlist yet score fairly on the Match tab.
evidence: pipeline/jobfit/matching.py:256-269 (seniority KO applies to WEIGHTS archetypes; 'unknown' skips it)
suggested_acceptance: poolEntryFromAnalysis uses the same fail-closed archetype resolution as resolveCandidate; a shared unit test pins both paths to identical archetypes for the same analysis payload.
l2_priority: Seed one analysis without v2Profile; compare its KO/rank on /api/jobs/[id]/candidates vs its Match-tab score for the same job.

title: Analysis-sourced reasoning gets no CV narrative — the prompt demands citing CV facts it never receives
expected: The reasoning prompt receives the candidate's real CV content (summary, experience highlights, work links) so the verdict can cite concrete, candidate-specific evidence — Petra's senior bar and the prompt's own instruction.
got: CandidateInput (the analysisSlug/inline path) carries only tags — no summary/experienceHighlights/workLinks fields exist on it — so reasoning_context feeds empty narrative fields while build_prompt instructs 'cite at least one concrete detail from experienceHighlights/summary'. Boilerplate or hallucination is the only way to comply. The Match tab auto-defaults to the analysis source when no profiles exist (MatchTab.tsx:44). Profile-sourced candidates are properly grounded (transform.py:192-193). Grounding: 6/8 profile path vs 4/8 analysis path.
suggested_acceptance: resolveCandidate maps the analysis payload's summary/experience highlights/links into CandidateInput (and candidateSignature covers them for cache correctness); analysis-sourced reasoning cites a fact present in the stored analysis.
l2_priority: Run 'Explain fit' for an analysis-sourced candidate: does the verdict invent specifics (hallucinated skill = Petra's blocker), or stay generic (senior-quality fail)?

title: SHIP-BAR (multi-tenancy): the shortlist/match chain reads the default workspace; jobs queries are tenant-blind
expected: Public product path: a workspace's shortlist ranks that workspace's candidates against that workspace's jobs; no cross-tenant reads.
got: buildCandidatePool() calls listProfileRecords/listAnalysisRecords with the DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_ID default; writeMatchInput→getProfileRecord likewise; getJob/listCorpusJobs have no workspace_id in their SQL at all. Meanwhile /api/matrix already threads await currentWorkspace() — the plumbing exists and one adjacent surface uses it. Under the single-workspace dev gate this is dormant (hence reachability: low today); in the multi-workspace product (env.md: real auth has multi-workspace tenancy) every tenant's scan ranks the default tenant's people.
scope_note: Ship-bar item for run 2026-07-02-full ('public product path'). Impact-ranked below every-run findings while the dev gate keeps kp single-workspace; becomes blocker-class at multi-tenant launch.
suggested_acceptance: /api/match, /api/match/reasoning and /api/jobs/[id]/candidates resolve the session workspace and thread it through candidate-pool/match-input; jobs gain tenant scoping or an explicit shared-corpus decision recorded in accepted-gaps.
l2_priority: Create a second workspace with distinct seeds; run the shortlist and match from it and record whose candidates rank.

title: Engine-emitted fragments render verbatim English in the Czech UI; deterministic reasoning fallback is English-only
expected: Petra's criterion: internal UI and generated reasoning render correctly in Czech.
got: The UI catalog is fully cs and the LLM narrative honors --lang cs (MAT1). But KO reason details ('seniority gap (…)'), confidence drivers ('Early-career: thinner, less-verifiable track record'), candidate assumptions, aggregate KO clauses, the pool-empty note, and the entire deterministic reasoning template are hardcoded English strings shown verbatim — so a degraded/keyless run serves an English rationale in a Czech session, and every shortlist carries English fragments.
suggested_acceptance: Engine emits stable keys for KO reasons/drivers/assumptions (the MatrixTab koKeys pattern, MatrixTab.tsx:77-87, already proves the approach) and the client localizes; deterministic reasoning template gains a cs variant or is routed through the lang directive.
l2_priority: Screenshot a cs-locale shortlist and a degraded reasoning panel; count untranslated strings a manager would see.

title: Shortlist card drops the per-dimension score breakdown it already receives; no score links to outcome calibration
expected: Kateřina's criterion: a match score is presented with its basis (what raised it, what capped it) and ideally a calibration reference — on the surface where the decision is made.
got: matching.build_score_breakdown ships weight-aware per-dimension contributions in every ranked row (recruiter.py model_dump), and the Match tab renders them; the Jobs-side CandidateCard renders only ScoreBadge + confidence + skills — the client CandResult type simply omits scoreBreakdown, so the basis data dies on the wire. Separately, CalibrationPanel (Analytics) exists with an honest minimum-outcomes gate, but no shortlist/match surface references it, and 0 outcome sources feed the scorer — the score is construction-legible but predictively unvalidated everywhere a recruiter sees it.
scope_note: Severity 'minor' because confidence drivers + matched/missing skills already give a partial basis on the card; impact ranks it high-frequency. Cheap fix: the data is already in the payload.
suggested_acceptance: The job-side candidate card renders the ScoreBreakdown (shared component) and the score badge links/tooltips to the calibration state once outcomes exist.
l2_priority: Confirm the breakdown is truly absent on the live card and the score→calibration path is unlinked end to end.

title: Empty candidate pool: the server's guidance note is dropped by the client — two bare empty columns, no chain to Analyze/Profile
expected: A fresh workspace's first scan explains that the pool is empty and links to the tabs that fill it (the Match tab's ChainEmptyState is the in-house pattern).
got: /api/jobs/[id]/candidates returns { candidates: [], note: 'No saved candidates yet.' }; RecruiterCandidates never reads `note` and renders two generic 'No candidates in this group' columns. The journey file explicitly flags this as an empty-state finding, not a pass.
scope_note: Overlaps backlog idea-7918a76c (chain-aware empty states) — still open, so not suppressed.
suggested_acceptance: Empty scan renders one chain-aware empty state linking to Analyze/Profile instead of two bare columns.
l2_priority: Fresh-workspace first-run: open a role's candidates tab with zero seeds and record what a new recruiter sees.

title: Pool caps (100 profiles + 60 analyses) silently exclude older candidates from every ranking; the warning is server-log-only
expected: If the ranked 'pool' is not the whole pool, the recruiter/sourcer sees that on the surface (count + who's excluded), because at bank scale (~100+ open roles) the cap will be routinely hit.
got: buildCandidatePool bounds the scan at PROFILE_POOL_CAP=100 + ANALYSIS_POOL_CAP=60 and console.warns on overflow — nothing reaches the UI; the shortlist header gives no 'ranked N of M' signal.
ceiling: Deliberate perf bound with a logged overflow — the gap is disclosure, not the cap itself.
scope_note: Low frequency with current fixtures; high at the target customer's scale — the kp-industry-locked class of gap.
suggested_acceptance: When a cap is hit, the candidates panel shows 'scored newest N of M candidates' with a paginate/raise-cap path.
l2_priority: Seed >160 candidates and confirm the UI says nothing while the log warns.

title: Degraded reasoning is labeled 'rule-based' but never says WHY (allowance exhausted vs missing key vs provider failure)
expected: When the verdict falls to the deterministic template, the recruiter can tell budget-degrade ('allowance used up — upgrades when it returns') from an outage, because the two demand different actions.
got: meterAllows('ai_candidates')=false pushes --no-llm — the same path a missing key or provider exception takes (match_reasoning.generate catch) — and the UI chip renders only 'pravidlové'/'rule-based' with no cause.
ceiling: The degrade itself is deliberate (docs/BILLING.md contract) and honestly labeled; only the cause is opaque.
suggested_acceptance: The source chip (or its tooltip) distinguishes 'allowance' from 'provider unavailable', reusing the meter state the server already knows.
l2_priority: Exhaust the ai_candidates allowance and screenshot what the recruiter is told.

title: Match-tab bulk shortlist gives no aggregate completion feedback (Matrix already fixed this pattern)
expected: After 'Add N to pipeline', a visible 'added X, failed Y' outcome — the completion band MatrixTab added because 'sighted users got nothing before'.
got: Results.addSelected updates per-card state and keeps failures selected, but emits no aria-live announce and no visible aggregate outcome; the Matrix bulk add has both.
suggested_acceptance: Match-tab bulk add reuses the Matrix lastAdd band + announce pattern.

title: Matrix and the Jobs candidates scan rank different populations for the same 'who fits this role' question
expected: Cross-surface reconciliation: the fit answer for a role is drawn from one candidate population, or the difference is stated.
got: Matrix scores listMatrixProfiles (v2 profiles only, cap 200) × open pipeline positions; the Jobs scan scores buildCandidatePool (profiles cap 100 + analyses cap 60) × any job. An analysis-only candidate ranks on the shortlist but is absent from the grid; caps differ; neither surface names the delta.
evidence: app/api/jobs/[id]/candidates/route.ts:17-19 (shared-pool comment claims the views 'never diverge' — true vs rediscovery, not vs Matrix)
suggested_acceptance: Matrix consumes the same buildCandidatePool population (or the grid states 'v2 profiles only — N analysis-based candidates not shown').
l2_priority: Same role via Matrix and via Jobs candidates: diff the ranked sets and count the missing analysis-only candidates.

title: STRENGTH — live-corpus hand-off on all three routes: a recruiter-ingested/published job ranks and reasons end to end
expected: DoD: an ingested job ranks too, not only the static seed corpus.
got: Structurally satisfied three ways: /api/match hands the DB corpus as --jobs-json (DB wins on id collision); the reasoning runner does the same and content-addresses the corpus into the cache key; the jobs candidates route passes the DB job record directly as --job-json.
l2_priority: Ingest a fresh ad, publish, scan, and 'Explain fit' against it — confirm the whole chain live (journey L2 item).

title: STRENGTH — reasoning cache correctness + honest degrade: 5-axis invalidation, fallbacks disclosed and never cached
expected: A cached verdict never survives a candidate edit, job edit, locale switch, or corpus change; a non-AI verdict is disclosed.
got: Cache key = prompt version × candidate content hash × job content hash × locale × corpus fingerprint, with CI pinning the prompt-version pair; deterministic fallbacks are labeled ('LLM' vs 'pravidlové' + cached suffix, localized) and stay uncached so they upgrade when the provider returns.
l2_priority: Confirm cached:true returns fast on a re-run and a cs session never serves an en cached verdict.

title: STRENGTH — provenance-honest, fairness-structural ranking: tracks, partial-match marking, KO/near-miss/skipped disclosure, auditable cross-scheme matrix with CSV
expected: No black-box list: every surfaced/excluded candidate carries an interrogable basis.
got: Early-career vs experienced are structurally separate tracks (never one incomparable total); partial matches marked '~' with strength %; skill provenance badges incl. observed; per-candidate KO reasons with near-miss flag; malformed candidates surfaced as skipped with reasons; robust-mean Fair Rank + full per-scheme fairness matrix exportable to CSV — the compliance artifact.
l2_priority: Panel check: does Fair Rank visibly reorder a real cohort, and does the CSV open clean in Excel (cs locale separators)?
